findings.title: value passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data is not the actual triggering value
findings.body: In evaluate_group_key_value, `value` is the raw group value passed into the method, but build_occurrence_and_event_data is called with this same `value` regardless of which condition triggered the status change. If multiple group keys/conditions are evaluated, this is fine per-call, but the occurrence creation logic has no access to which specific condition/threshold triggered `new_status`, making it hard for subclasses to build accurate occurrence data (e.g. evidence_data) that reflects the triggering comparison. This is a design limitation that silently loses information needed for a correct occurrence.

findings.title: Removed duplicate detector_group_key validation without replacement safeguard
findings.body: The previous code detected and logged duplicate group_key results returned from handler.evaluate() to catch handler bugs producing duplicate state entries. Now that evaluate returns a dict, duplicates are structurally impossible from a single handler call, which is reasonable, but the removal means any pre-existing/legacy handler returning overlapping keys across multiple invocations/retries silently overwrites prior results with no logging, losing visibility into misbehaving handlers that was previously present via logger.error. This could hide real duplication bugs if a handler indirectly produces colliding keys via other code paths before conversion to a dict occurs upstream.

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits abstract StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing abstract methods
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but provides no implementation for the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data (all declared via @abc.abstractmethod in detector.py). Since the class body is just `pass`, instantiating MetricAlertDetectorHandler will raise a TypeError at runtime (Python enforces abstract method implementation), breaking any code path that calls `detector.detector_handler` for a Detector of type metric_alert_fire. This is a functional regression compared to the previous version, which at least implemented a concrete (if stubbed) evaluate method via DetectorHandler.
